references.text: Joshua gave orders to take twelve stones from the Jordan, which are now being set up at Gilgal
The Israelites did as Joshua commanded and took twelve stones from the Jordan, one for each tribe
Joshua also set up twelve stones in the middle of the Jordan where the priests stood with the ark of the covenant
The people came up out of the Jordan and camped at Gilgal, the place where the stones were set up
Gilgal became an important place for Israel, where they were also circumcised after crossing over
Moses set up twelve pillars for the twelve tribes of Israel at the covenant of Sinai, a similar memorial
Twelve stones on the high priest's breastplate represented the twelve tribes of Israel
Jacob set up a stone as a pillar in Bethel, a similar act to remember God's intervention
